question.worked_solution:
The formula for the derivative of the inverse hyperbolic cosecant function is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcsch}⁡x)=-\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{1+{x}^{2}}}.
$$

Using the formula above with the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({e}^{4x}-2\operatorname{arcsch}⁡{e}^{2x}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({e}^{4x})-2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcsch}⁡{e}^{2x}) \\  & =4{e}^{4x}-2(-\frac{1}{|{e}^{2x}|\sqrt{1+({e}^{2x})^{2}}})\cdot ({e}^{2x})^{′} \\  & =4{e}^{4x}+\frac{2}{{e}^{2x}\sqrt{1+{e}^{4x}}}\cdot 2{e}^{2x} \\  & =4{e}^{4x}+\frac{4}{\sqrt{1+{e}^{4x}}} \\  & =4({e}^{4x}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+{e}^{4x}}}).\end{aligned}
$$
